items.summary: Binance 对 OKX 的 PEPE 溢价快照约67基点，ENA约24基点。BitHappy建议仅用两所已有库存，在 Binance 卖、OKX买来锁差，不为套利新充值；单边持仓不算对锁。价差随提现恢复可能收窄，第三方数据不能证明买家就是 Binance，下单须核实时价。

evidence.quote: Since the hack, Binance trades at a premium to OKX on the tokens the attacker reportedly sold: PEPE +67 bps, ENA +24, UNI +17, WLD +17. Before, the gap was under 3 bps on all 13 tokens we track.
Binance says it is buying the last 20% of losses "through market and OTC". The gap fits that demand. Public data can't show who is buying
现在提币没完全恢复，搬砖的币进不来、出不去，价差才挂得住。所以这个价差的寿命，很大程度上绑在提现恢复的节奏上。
1/ 两边本来就有库存：在币安卖、在 OKX 买回，不用转账，就能把价差锁住，等恢复后再慢慢平衡库存；
2/ 只有一边有货：做不了真正的对锁，只是在赌方向，这不算搬砖；
个人认为最好的取舍是：只用现有库存锁价差，不为它新充值进币安。
3/ 基点数是快照，盘口随时在变，下单前以实时价格为准。

items.author: evanjconrad
items.event: 算力信用紧缩下的投资结构
items.new_information: 提出VC持有算力换股权，以及企业浮动定价和可中断服务的应对框架

evidence.quote: right now you are being asked for a near 100% prepayment because neither you nor the cloud is considered credit worthy, and so nobody can get debt. As ai scales, we are asking the credit markets to take on a massive single sector deployment of capital. More money deployed, more scared everyone gets.

the “market” is working on solving it. We know, because we are the market, and we’re working on it. sfcompute is working on ways of firming up the collateral of the loans, which makes it safer to lend to a startup.

first, venture firms need to understand that they are in the compute business now and deploying capital to pay for a 100% prepayment for 10 startups where 6 of them die and 4 of them make 50% margins on that capital is basically locking in non-venture returns. many funds, via low understanding of the space, are wrecking their funds.

there’s an economic solution for vc’s and it is owning the compute and trading equity for gpu/hrs. If the company dies, you keep the residual value. Each of you are looking to capture the next anthropic or openai, but the only way these companies scaled was by trading compute for equity.

The second is to design your business model to support variable priced tokens and compute. As the financial ecosystem builds around compute, you will be able to trade “lower up front payments” for “variably priced compute or tokens”. Your business will get tailwinds from the infra under you if you setup your business model such that YOUR customers have

variable prices and you’re just adding a % take rate on top of the underlying floating price. Every year, you will become more and more capital efficient. The economic winners in ai & inference are firms that make lower and lower margin every year, but become more capital efficient & scale faster every year, making their gross profit increase.

The third option is asynchronous or interrupted products. If you have a variable cogs, but a fixed rate card for your customers, it can’t have 100% availability or you’ll go bankrupt. But it is totally possible to design your product such that customers like this.

items.new_information: 回购笔数近三倍但金额仅增约800美元，新增产品采用及留存观察框架

evidence.quote: Looking at the data, during our previous analysis, the website showed 2,808 unique .ai Agent ID wallets that had bought at least one launchpad token. Cumulative burns stood at 5.11 million GANG, representing 0.511% of the total supply. Total buybacks were approximately $31,500 across 295 transactions, while the treasury held around $7,878.

In the latest snapshot, the number of wallets had increased to 3,478, cumulative burns reached 7.41 million GANG, or 0.741% of the total supply, buyback transactions increased to 836, cumulative buybacks reached approximately $32,300, and the treasury grew to around $8,880. Wallet participation and token burns are both increasing. However, buyback

transactions have nearly tripled while the total buyback value has only increased by roughly $800. This suggests that buybacks are happening more frequently, but the actual amount of capital being deployed has not expanded at the same rate.

However, trading volume is not the same as net capital inflow, and short-term turnover does not prove that these projects can survive over the long term. The next thing to watch is whether they can maintain liquidity and trading activity.

The key metrics I will be watching are the actual adoption of Bond Mode, real MCP usage, and whether graduated projects can maintain meaningful trading activity one week or even one month after launch.

items.summary: Anthropic让数千个Claude Agent生成可绕过审查的训练数据：看似正常的养蜂问答、摔角故事也能诱发被微调模型的不安全行为。实验模型未部署，真实训练环境中的攻击效果尚未证实。
items.author: AnthropicAI
items.event: Anthropic自动化训练数据红队实验
items.new_information: Agent生成表面无害但能诱发失配的训练数据，现实有效性仍待验证

evidence.quote: Red-teaming is a vital part of model safety testing, but it’s also limited by researchers’ time. To see if we could automate it, we set thousands of Claude agents the task of evading a training data monitor.

These agents developed training data that looked harmless to monitors (like a veteran wrestler mentoring a newcomer, or a Q&A about professional beekeeping), but that in fact taught misaligned behavior.

Examples like these can be used to directly improve future training data monitors. This research is only a first step, but it suggests that future red-teaming efforts could improve much further, using better models and more compute.
当然，实验有很强的人工设计成分，模型也从未真正部署。Anthropic 还不能证明这种攻击在真实训练环境中同样有效。

items.summary: Raw-RAG论文在四类记忆基准、七组模型设置中拿下六组第一，比最强对比方案高0.13–5.53个百分点。方法保留原始历史并检索重排；分析认为摘要化可能损失时序、关系及依赖路径。
items.author: Xudong07452910
items.new_information: 多组基准中原始历史检索胜出，指出记忆压缩可能损失关系证据

evidence.quote: Raw-RAG 的方法非常简单：
保留原始对话历史，切成带重叠的文本块；先做 dense retrieval，再用 reranker 筛一遍，最后把最相关的原始证据交给 LLM 推理。
中间没有 LLM 摘要、记忆重写、UPDATE / DELETE，也没有复杂的图结构。
结果在 LoCoMo、LongMemEval、MEME 和 MemoryAgentBench 上，7 组模型设置里拿下 6 组第一，比最强的对比 Memory 系统高 0.13–5.53 个百分点。
很多问题真正需要的证据，并不只是某个「答案值」，还包括时间顺序、前后关系和依赖路径。
Memory 一旦把历史压缩成独立事实或摘要，这些关系很容易在整理过程中被削弱。甚至把完整的 transformed memory 全部交给模型，效果依然和直接看 raw evidence 存在差距。

evidence.quote: Think about how your laptop stays cool. A little fan blows air over the chip and the air carries the heat away. Big data centers do the same thing on a massive scale, with water pipes running out to cooling towers. All of it works because there's air and water around to soak up the heat. Up in orbit there's basically nothing. A vacuum is one of the best
insulators there is, which is the whole reason your thermos keeps coffee hot all day.
So the only way a satellite can get rid of heat is to glow it off.

Google's test satellite is about the size of a fridge. It has four of Google's AI chips on board and solar panels that make around one kilowatt, roughly what your microwave pulls. Even on that little power, the chips can't run nonstop. They work for about 15 minutes, then shut off and wait for the radiators to catch up. The haiku Sundar posted came out of

SpaceX has filed for a million satellites of its own, and Starship keeps pushing the price of a launch down. Cheaper launches mean you can afford to send up bigger radiators, and whoever builds the lightest radiator that dumps the most heat is going to own AI in orbit. For now, the satellite in Sundar's video still has to stop and cool down every 15 minutes
or so.

evidence.quote: According to The Wall Street Journal, Arini Capital Management has been forced to sell roughly $800 MILLION worth of debt holdings in recent weeks after suffering massive losses and facing margin calls from its banks. For some context, Arini’s flagship fund manages approximately $7 billion and was already down more than 20% this year as of mid-October, with

Arini made some aggressive bets on distressed debt, essentially lending to or buying the debt of financially struggling companies at discounted prices, hoping to make substantial profits when those companies recovered or restructured. A lot of those bets were concentrated in telecommunications companies like Altice, Optimum, Virgin Media, and Brightspeed.

Arini was using leverage, meaning it had borrowed money or taken on leveraged exposure to amplify its investment returns. As the value of its positions declined, banks started demanding additional collateral through margin calls.
That means Arini couldn’t necessarily afford to just sit around and wait for these investments to recover. It had to raise cash, including by selling investments that were easier to unload.

This can create a dangerous cycle. Investments lose value, banks demand more collateral, funds are forced to sell assets, and those sales can put even more downward pressure on prices. If enough highly leveraged funds are holding similar positions, the selling can spread throughout the credit market.

evidence.quote: 2) we should have just done the airdrop pro rata instead of using the ARP score.  there's two conflicting arguments here:

B (against ARP): the airdrop goals should not have been "calculate a distribution that scientifically predicts who will hold."  given we ran an airdrop campaign, the implicit expectation of players is that they'd be rewarded tokens based on their points.  everything that we "fixed" with the distribution (punishing sybils, cheating, exploits, botting, wash

trading) was done retroactively instead of just straight up banning these players early on.  what we ended up doing over the past few years was create an environment and community culture that harbored these players, with only sporadic enforcement of rules.  thus, they have a rational counterpoint that 1) their continued engagement benefited us, 2) that many

were forced to engage in these behaviors to remain competitive, 3) that they were not told ahead of time that this could be a consequence, and 4) getting "vibe-filtered" actually led to them selling it all in rage, instead of the other way around.  ultimately, the ARP ended up not changing distribution much (~12% of the tokens shifted as a result of ARP)
while creating unnecessary FUD, confusion, uncertainty, and division within the community.

at the current moment, i don't think dwelling on these issues too long is a good use of our time - we should be laser focused on shipping genesis and growing the protocol, any more time spent here is massively expensive in terms of opportunity cost.  however, I do want to eventually revisit and correct the two biggest imbalances (duel arena / gold rush s3

weighting, and token allocation lost to ARP scores specifically due to nft selling) at some point in the future when there's more value to distribute.  this will not be in additional tokens (it's too late for that, tokens are scaling units of value).  but more in terms of adjusting for the value of the slashed tokens at time of TGE.

items.summary: Google真实安全通知也可能夹带钓鱼内容：案例中攻击者把恐吓文字和短链接写入应用密码名称，再转发Google签名邮件，DKIM与DMARC仍通过。识别点是通知指向他人账户，“24小时后永久访问”的说法也不实。
items.author: 0xkeenz
items.event: Google安全通知被利用进行钓鱼
items.new_information: 新增通过真实签名邮件夹带恶意文本的手法及账户归属识别点

evidence.quote: Just got a phishing email that Gmail authenticated as Google. DKIM/DMARC passed. I can see a lot of people falling for this one, since it plays to the idea that your account has already been compromised.

1. The trick: The attacker puts the threatening text and shortened URL into an app password’s customizable name on another account. Google incorporates that text into a real security notification and signs the email.
2. The delivery: That notification is forwarded through another mailbox to the victim. In this message, Gmail still recorded passing Google DKIM and DMARC authentication.

3. What makes it convincing: The Google sender, signature, branding, and “Check activity” button are legitimate. The suspected attacker-supplied text appears inside the same trusted-looking template, using a deadline to push you toward its separate link.
4. The giveaway: Both the notification and its genuine Google button refer to someone else’s account. The “permanent access after 24 hours” claim is false; app passwords can be revoked.
